business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Supply of Drummed and Bagged Penetration Grade Bitumen

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong reliance on statutory law and codified obligations; federal and cantonal bifurcation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1996, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SR 220 – Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, Arts. 626, 911a et seq.); SR 955.0 – Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA); SR 955.01 – Ordinance on the Federal Act (AMLO); SR 221.411 – Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); SR 946.03 – Embargo Act (Bundesgesetz über die Durchsetzung von internationalen Sanktionen).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior management against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) sanctions list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (autonomous adoption in Switzerland is dynamic), OFAC SDN/consolidated list (referenced as a best-practice standard), plus domestic PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies for any foreign PEP holding direct or indirect control of the legal entity, requiring exhaustion of source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation in accordance with FINMA circular 2023/1 and AMLA Article 6a.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be legally permissible in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh). A foreign-language name is accepted only where it is not deceptive and where the name clearly identifies the company and its legal form. For non-Latin script, an official transliteration/romanisation is mandatory and must be identical to the registered foreign business name. The company name must be distinguished from all existing registered names; trademarks and public-law entitlements are also taken into account.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bitumen / Asphalt (if combined with misleading geographic or quality references)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed company name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (Einsprache/Beschwerde) with the cantonal commercial register supervision authority within 30 days of the rejection decision. The appeal must state the grounds for contesting the refusal. If the cantonal review is unsuccessful, a further appeal may be lodged with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days, and ultimately the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) on constitutional law grounds. Interim name-reservation extensions can be requested prior to the expiry of the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office is not acceptable as a substitute for the legal registered office in Switzerland. The company must have a physical office within the canton of registration, where it maintains actual administrative and management activities. Serviced or shared offices are permissible only if the company conclusively demonstrates that the registered address is the centre of its de facto administration and that personnel, books and records, and management functions are practically located there. For bitumen/asphalt wholesale logistics (ISIC 4661), no pure virtual or mailbox address will satisfy the commercial substance test for obtaining cantonal authority approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified annual risk of an unannounced on-site inspection for a standard low-risk wholesale trading company is approximately 8-10%. However, if the AG has a non-resident board, no operational personnel in Switzerland, or exhibits symptoms of a pure invoice-trader (no logistics, no inventory documentation), the probability of a cantonal tax or commercial register physical inspection rises to 30-40% within the first two years. Additional targeted inspections may be triggered by incomplete AML/UBO filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620-763 for the Aktiengesellschaft; Articles 629-638 for incorporation procedure; Articles 64-651 regarding audits; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Articles 1, 26-36, 98-101; Swiss Civil Code Article 52 on legal personality.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug); federal supervising and appeal body: Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA/OFREG), Bern.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung der Statuten) with joint declaration of founding shareholders (Erklärung der Gründung) and registered application for entry (Gründungsanmeldung) submitted electronically via the canton's regix/CH web interface.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum issued share capital; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash (minimum 20% of each share) and deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank, with the bank's release confirmation filed with the Commercial Register; non-cash contributions (Sacheinlagen) require an audit report and full immediate payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company adopts the Articles of Association authenticated by public deed and accepts subscription of 100 fully paid-up registered shares at CHF 1,000 par value each, comprising the entire CHF 100,000 share capital, with at least CHF 50,000 deposited in a Swiss bank blocked escrow account for release upon commercial registry confirmation. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Association in the Canton of Zug, Switzerland, and the Commercial Register and tax authorities are notified accordingly. RESOLVED, that the directors named in the instrument are appointed, external auditors engaged, and any one director together with the Chairman is authorized to sign the registration application and execute all ancillary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed notary public (Öffentliche/r Notar/in) authorized in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuten (German/French/English) containing the corporate name, registered office in the Canton of Zug, purpose limited to wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen, share capital structure, board powers, and auditor appointment. Verify founding shareholders' identities, execute the deed before the notary, and obtain certified copies plus the electronic notarized instrument for registry upload.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association draft (Statuten)
Valid passport or national ID of each founding shareholder and director
Proof of legal capacity and payment clearance for corporate founders
Declaration of acceptance and consent to act signed by each director
Consent of designated external auditor (where required)
Draft registration application (Gründungsanmeldung) signed by founders and board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the deed, amend the Articles by supplementary notarial declaration and re-authenticate; any corrective filing restarts only the affected portions of the register application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Share Capital Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or cantonal bank licensed by FINMA (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or a private banker in Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the company to be incorporated (CH_AG in Gründung), deposit at least CHF 50,000 of cash contributions by each subscribing shareholder, and instruct the bank to issue the formal shareholder funds confirmation (Bankbestätigung über liberierte Einlagen) stating that funds are blocked until the Commercial Register entry and are at the free disposal of the Board thereafter.
required_dossiers: Provisional incorporation deed and draft Articles
Share subscription list and payment orders from each shareholder
Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
Passports or IDs of beneficial owners
Compliance form on source of funds (due diligence requirements)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the confirmation, supplement the deposit amount or substitute an acceptable bank; reissue the escrow confirmation once full statutory payment is reached.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed and registration application electronically or in person; ensure all directors have Swiss or recognized foreign residence arrangements; the registry reviews the deed, capital confirmation, and consents; upon approval, the company receives its UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and the registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt).
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and Articles of Association
Electronic registration form signed by directors
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital in blocked account
Auditor consent (if applicable)
Tax clearance certificate for companies with taxable substance
Identification documents of all directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or provisional refusal, cure defects by submitting revised documents within 30 days; appeal a final refusal to the Cantonal Economic Department and further to the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Cantonal Tax and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT; Cantonal Tax Authority of Zug (Kantonales Steueramt Zug); Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse) for AHV/IV/EO
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registry entry, the UID is automatically issued by the Federal Statistical Office. File mandatory VAT registration with the ESTV if annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, or voluntarily for lower turnover; register the company with the Zug compensation fund for social security contributions of any employees, and submit the corporate tax opening declaration to the cantonal tax administration.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract and UID notification
Articles of Association and board resolution for tax representation
VAT registration form (RC) for the trading activity
Employer registration form and staff declarations
Cantonal tax questionnaire for real estate and capital tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations can be cured by filing backdated declarations with penalty waivers for good faith; object to VAT assessment within 30 days and request abatement of procedural fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Governance and Opening of Commercial Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of CH_AG; Swiss financial intermediary (bank) for operating accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first full board meeting to adopt the board regulations (Organisationsreglement), issue share certificates to shareholders, release the blocked escrow funds, open current trading accounts for letter-of-credit and wire operations, appoint banking signatories, and minutes all resolutions; maintain the share ledger and submit beneficial ownership filings to the FINMA-compiled register if statutory thresholds apply.
required_dossiers: Full meeting minutes of the first board organizational meeting
Share certificates and subscription list
Bank escrow release instruction and new account agreements
Registration extract as proof of legal personality
Signatory identification and authorization sheets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective organizational acts are ratified by subsequent board resolution; missing filings with the economic interest register are corrected immediately upon discovery with a note of intentional cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Physical Site Clearance for Drummed Bitumen Storage
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Fire Prevention Authority (Feuerpolizei Zug), Cantonal Building Inspectorate, and Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical office and any bonded or covered warehouse storing drummed and bagged bitumen, obtain fire certification for racking and drum storage, verify structural floor loadings, notify the environmental office for packaged hazardous goods, and complete Suva occupational safety clearance for handling bituminous products; no separate federal industrial manufacturing permit is required for pure wholesale trading.
required_dossiers: Fire safety concept and site plan for warehouse
Structural load calculation for storage racks and mezzanines
Emergency response and spill containment plan
Suva occupational safety checklist (handling of bitumen drums)
Environmental notification form for packaged goods warehouse
Building occupancy permit for commercial use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If inspections reveal deficiencies, implement remedial works within the stated deadline and submit an amended compliance dossier; temporary occupancy permits may be granted pending full certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Industry Inspectorate of Zug (Gewerbeinspektorat Zug) in coordination with the Cantonal Building and Economic Development Office; federal supervision by the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/OFEV)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit is statutorily required for wholesale supply and containerized trading of bitumen; a building occupancy certificate and warehouse operations approval are applicable only when physically storing drummed or bagged bitumen.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/OFEV) and Cantonal Environmental Agency of Zug (Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal Environmental Impact Assessment (UVP/EIA) for covered warehouse storage of packaged bitumen products below the Annex thresholds of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV); a low-tier environmental register notification and standard building permit clearance apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewers compliant with the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 3.2; no VOC emissions from cold storage of drummed bitumen, but if melting or heating occurs, compliance with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) Annex 3 emission limits is required; bitumen spills must be contained and disposed as non-hazardous or hazardous waste per the Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VEVA); occupational exposure limit for bitumen fumes at 10 mg/m3 per Suva limit values.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Zug Fire Prevention Authority covering drum storage racks and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate for warehouse flooring; Suva workplace safety clearance for manual handling of drums, hot bitumen risks, and hazardous substance training; civil defense shelter contribution requirements and CO2 emission documentation as applicable to the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Federal Tax Administration FTA), Main Division Value Added Tax; associated registry authorities include the Federal Statistical Office (UID register) and the Cantonal Commercial Registers. Official portals: www.estv.admin.ch, www.uid.admin.ch, www.zefix.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss-incorporated Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) Notarize the Articles and register the AG in the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister); the company automatically obtains a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer; format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) from the Federal Statistical Office. (2) Upon commencing taxable activities in Switzerland, submit a VAT registration application to the ESTV/FTA Main Division VAT within 30 days using the ESTV e-Service portal; attach the Commercial Register excerpt, Articles of Association, business activity description and beneficial-owner declaration. (3) The statutory VAT ID is the UID with the suffix MWST (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST); the plain UID serves as the corporate income tax file reference at federal and cantonal levels. (4) Foreign entities without a Swiss registered office or Swiss branch performing taxable supplies in Switzerland must register directly with the ESTV under the non-established-taxpayer route; the CHF 100,000 turnover exemption does not apply to foreign non-established suppliers; the foreign registrant must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (domiciliary agent) authorized to receive ESTV decisions and is jointly and severally liable for Swiss VAT debts. Because the CH_AG is a resident entity, domestic registration applies and no separate PE/branch registration is required where its Sitz and place of effective management are in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The Swiss AG is a separate taxable person subject to federal corporate income tax (statutory 8.5% of after-tax profit; effective approximately 7.8% of pre-tax profit) plus cantonal/communal profit tax (aggregate typical burden approximately 12%-21% depending on canton; Zug approx. 11.9%) and cantonal capital tax; resident AGs have unlimited worldwide tax liability subject to exemption with progression for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate; no pass-through eligibility; no tax-exempt zone status; for VAT purposes the AG is a taxable person by law unless the small-business exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; Swiss tax classification follows Swiss corporate legal form (Handelsregister). Statutory elections available to this structure include: (a) VAT group taxation (Art. 21 MWSTG) for Swiss enterprises with financial, economic and organizational integration; binding for at least one five-year fiscal surveillance period and requires ESTV approval; (b) voluntary VAT registration by a business below the CHF 100,000 threshold; (c) cash-basis VAT accounting election (Art. 36 MWSTG) where prior-year turnover does not exceed approximately CHF 5.0 million; (d) tracking of capital contribution reserves to preserve privileged Swiss withholding-tax treatment on future distributions; (e) no elective hybrid-mismatch regime; Art. 58a DBG contains a mandatory unilateral anti-hybrid rule disallowing interest deductions for hybrid financing producing double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 net taxable turnover sourced in Switzerland per calendar year (Art. 10 MWSTG; CHF 150,000 for non-profit, sporting or cultural institutions). Non-established foreign suppliers have a nil threshold: any taxable supply with a Swiss place of supply mandates Swiss VAT registration. Import VAT on goods entering the Swiss customs territory arises irrespective of taxpayer turnover and is administered by the Federal Customs Administration (Art. 50 MWSTG).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-approval API or digital stamping regime exists in Switzerland. Invoicing may be in paper or electronic form; the ESTV accepts PDF, XML and the Swiss eBill standard. Structured electronic invoicing (PDF/XML, EDIFACT/INVOIC) is mandatory only for invoices to the Swiss federal administration (B2G, since 1 January 2020). Private-sector e-invoicing is optional but common. Fiscal books, vouchers, customs declarations and export evidence must be retained for 10 years (Art. 70 MWSTG; Art. 958f CO).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported out of the Swiss customs territory qualify for VAT-exempt treatment with input VAT deduction, i.e. the economic equivalent of zero-rating (Art. 23 MWSTG), where: (i) the goods are physically dispatched or carried to a foreign destination; (ii) the supply is made to the foreign purchaser in a commercial transaction; (iii) export is proved by a Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration via e-dec/NCTS) accepted by the Federal Customs Administration; and (iv) transport documents (ocean/multimodal bill of lading, CMR, air waybill) show dispatch from Switzerland. Drummed and bagged penetration-grade bitumen sold by the CH_AG on EXW/FCA/FOB terms for containerized overseas shipment is zero-rated when the goods leave Switzerland in the same fiscal period. Services directly related to exported goods (international transport, freight forwarding, insurance, loading and inspection) are zero-rated under Arts. 24-25 MWSTG. Services supplied to recipients whose seat is abroad are outside Swiss VAT scope under Art. 7 MWSTG, so wholesale trading commissions and management margins do not attract Swiss VAT. Imported bitumen may be held in customs-warehouse suspension (Art. 30 MWSTG) so that import VAT is discharged by the subsequent zero-rated export; alternatively import VAT at 8.1% is recoverable as input VAT by the fully taxable AG.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss e-dec / Ausfuhrdeklaration with customs office acceptance reference; NCTS/T1 transit evidence for movements via EU/EFTA territory; exit confirmation from the Swiss customs territory for containerized ocean shipments).

Bill of Lading (original ocean or multimodal B/L showing Swiss container terminal as port of loading and a foreign port of discharge, consigned or endorsed to the overseas buyer; container and seal numbers must match the customs declaration).

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank payment confirmation, SWIFT MT103 or TT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer; required under the compliance pipeline treasury rule for FX repatriation within 180 days from date of export).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV/FTA verifies export evidence arithmetically against VAT returns. Where export proof is missing, incomplete or contradictory, zero-rating is denied and the supply becomes taxable at 8.1% with default interest at 4.5% per annum; assessments may be reopened within a 10-year statutory limitation period (Art. 42 MWSTG). Tax evasion (Art. 96 MWSTG) attracts a penalty surcharge of up to three times the VAT evaded; procedural-duty violations (Art. 100 MWSTG) may draw fines up to CHF 8,000; fraudulent documentation may additionally trigger penalties under the Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR). Non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days does not mechanically invalidate zero-rating under Swiss statutory VAT law, but it constitutes a high-scrutiny audit trigger that leads to validation of underlying export documents, beneficial-ownership facts and any intercompany financing, and may indirectly expose the transaction to reassessment and penalties if the commercial substance of the export is not fully substantiated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); in respect of sanctions and export controls, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) administers financial sanctions and export-related restrictions, while the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) licenses and supervises banks and securities firms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full and unrestricted convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no approval requirement for profit or dividend remittances, and no restrictions on opening or funding CHF or foreign-currency accounts by non-residents. The sole structural hurdle is Swiss federal withholding tax of 35% on ordinary dividends or non-reportable interest paid to non-banking beneficiaries, which can be reduced or refunded under an applicable double-tax treaty; the accounting profit itself remains freely transferable after the withholding tax certificate is cleared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold receipts in any currency, use them to settle trade payables, or convert them freely. Institutional reporting obligations involve only the SNB's quarterly international payments statistics and monthly bank balance sheet statistics, collected by the intermediary bank, not the exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Blocked Account for Trade Collateralisation
Operational Transaction Account with Trade Finance Umbrella
Operational Current Account (CHF only unless given multi-currency mandate)
Operational Account for Commodity Trading and Documentary Collections
Capital Escrow Account for Private-Clients-linked Wealth Structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary bank account. A non-Swiss electronic money institution (EMI) or digital payment platform cannot execute payment services in Switzerland without a FINMA licence, a passport under EU-UK equivalence (generally unavailable), or a formal agency-banking arrangement with a licensed Swiss bank. For a bitumen wholesale trader, a foreign EMI may be viable only for low-value collections from known counterparties; it should not be used for capital escrow, LC settlement, or significant trade disbursements due to sanctions exposure and limited recourse.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Generally required. Corporate account onboarding requires at least one authorised signatory director or the appointed attorney-in-fact to appear physically before the relationship manager or a notary/consular officer. Pure remote video-only onboarding is generally not permitted for new corporate clients with complex trade structures; Swiss banks demand original apostilled board resolutions, certified articles of association, extract from the Commercial Register, and in many cases an in-person interview at the bank branch or a Swiss consulate for non-resident controllers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade lane involves countries in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) grey list or Swiss sanctions enforcement zones, notably Russia and Belarus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defensive bundle: ICC arbitration clause, Incoterms-specific sales contract, end-user certificate, carrier's compliance letter, vessel/VGM data, comprehensive CommodityTradeTransaction file, OFAC/SECO/FINRA sanction screening report, UBO register extract from the Swiss Commercial Register, and certified IDs/passports of the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate transaction turnover relative to stated paid-up capital of the Swiss AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defensive bundle: audited financial statements for the last two years, shareholder capital contribution certificate, Swiss certified public accountant's comfort letter, projected rolling 12-month trade finance facility and cash-flow statement, signed board resolution authorising the treasury mandate, and the underlying LC/bank agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual ownership chain or nominee/shareholder-fiduciary arrangement triggers PEP and source-of-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defensive bundle: Swiss Commercial Register extract showing ultimate beneficial owner, notarised declaration of trust defining no nominee relationship, source-of-wealth analysis (asset-and-liability statement, sale or inheritance agreements, audited financial statements of parent), PEP due-diligence questionnaire, and independent external counsel legal opinion confirming compliance with Art. 4 ff. of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment instructions routed through a non-Swiss intermediary or to a personal account in a third country for bitumen settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defensive bundle: full chain-of-trade documents (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, weight certificate), SWIFT MT103 messages matching LC terms, signed confirmation that the receiving account belongs solely to the contracting seller, KYC-checked buyer corporate registration, and a data-protection-compliant transaction audit trail for 10 years.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a capital increase or shareholder loan to the Swiss AG: (i) route the remittance as SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the parent company's bank to the Swiss bank account, using the beneficiary account field reserved for the AG's capital escrow account and the purpose text 'Unrestricted capital contribution under Art. 621 / Art. 632 Code of Obligations'; the SWIFT Instruction Identification should optionally carry code 'EQUI' or an equivalent ISO 20022 external purpose code designated by the receiving bank. (ii) Funds are credited within one business day under the Swiss SIC interbank system for the CHF leg, or via Target2 for EUR/other currencies. (iii) No SNB regulatory approval is required for a capital injection, but the bank will conduct a KYC/AML threshold check on the provenance of funds, and a CHF and foreign-currency cash position report may be submitted to the SNB as part of the bank's periodic statistical reporting when cumulative flows exceed materiality thresholds. (iv) For over CHF 10 million, provide a copy of the notarised capital-increase resolution and the Swiss Commercial Register notice to avoid frozen funds status.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For containerized bitumen/asphalt trades: (i) open-account settlements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 to the seller's bank with purpose code 'TREA' or 'TRAD' and the full commercial invoice reference; for sums above EUR/USD clearing thresholds or for time-critical payments, use MT202 cover with a SWIFT member bank. (ii) Documentary credits for bitumen cargoes are issued by SWIFT MT700 and advised through a Swiss trade-finance desk; settlement is effected via MT756 and MT202 when documents are presented; a standby LC (MT760) can secure prepayment. (iii) Swiss banks commonly request a 'Trade Services and Finance' umbrella, and all disbursements must match the reference in Part 6 of the LC application; cash advance disbursements must be linked either to letter-of-credit confirmation or to an approved export-credit insurance. (iv) SIC/Target2 and SWIFT are the physical clearing rails; no foreign-exchange benchmark approval is needed for seamless EUR/USD disbursements from CHF accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, EUR/USD)
Currency swaps (FX swaps) for managing rolling liquidity and short-dated cost of carry
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) when the settlement currency is an illiquid or restricted currency
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY) for structurally hedging trade-finance liabilities
Exchange-traded FX futures on Eurex (EUR/USD or CHF/USD) for liquid reduction of directional exposure
European-style FX options (plain vanilla calls and puts) to hedge tender/bid risk without booked forward obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; no filing to the Swiss Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date under Art. 698 CO; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered convocation on shareholder application; director liability for failure to present annual accounts; no annual administrative strike-off solely for this default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Commercial Register update notifications (no annual return is required for AGs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Only upon changes in directors, auditor, registered office, share capital, articles or liquidation; no fixed annual renewal date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex officio rectification and fines under Art. 943 CO; failure to remedy defective organization may lead to judicial dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and annual financial statements for tax assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for federal direct tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal calendar, generally between 31 March and 30 June for a 31 December year-end, with extensions permitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Estimated assessment, default interest, procedural fines and enforcement through cantonal tax collection; no commercial register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT period; annual filers with a 31 December period must file by early March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest and VAT penalties; summary fine up to CHF 8,000 per tax period for negligence, with criminal proceedings in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register review and confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office and statutory books; inspection rights limited to courts, tax and AML authorities on request; no public annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually at the balance-sheet date and immediately upon any change in beneficial ownership under Art. 697j CO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board personal liability and criminal fines for incorrect or omitted UBO entries; no commercial register strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit by an independent Swiss audit firm is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of these three thresholds for two consecutive years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million annual turnover, 250 full-time employees. Other AGs require a limited audit unless shareholders validly opt out under Art. 727a(2) CO, available only where the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-962) and Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS/IAS permitted for statutory financial statements and required for certain listed or regulated financial entities under FINMA rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The AG must identify and record every natural person who directly or indirectly holds at least 25% of shares or voting rights, controls 25% of voting rights by agreement, or has 25% economic entitlement. The register must be updated immediately after each share transfer or change in beneficial ownership and confirmed by the board at least annually before the annual general meeting. Transfers of registered shares are entered in the Aktienbuch only after proof of acquisition and appropriate UBO declaration; unregistered transfers do not confer membership rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 10,000 for limited audit; USD 18,000 - 50,000 for ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal direct profit tax (applied to net profit after tax, equivalent to 7.83% of pre-tax profit); cantonal and municipal corporate income taxes are additional and vary by canton. In the canton of Zug, the combined federal/cantonal/municipal effective rate for a stock company is approximately 14.6% of pre-tax profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Incentives available under the Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF/Federal Act 2020): patent box with up to 90% qualifying IP income relief; research and development super-deduction of up to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditure; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on participations; deemed interest deduction is not generally available. OECD Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) top-up tax of 15% applies from 2024 for multinational groups with EUR 750 million or more consolidated revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen'; in Zug, the form for AG/SA is filed through the official Zug online e-filing portal 'ezug' at www.zg.ch). The federal direct tax liability is assessed in the same cantonal return and remitted through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) coordination.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the financial year. For an AG with a 31 December balance-sheet date, the return is generally due by 30 June of the following year in most cantons; extensions are available upon reasoned application to the cantonal tax authority. For a non-calendar business year, the six-month period runs from the date of the annual balance-sheet closing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: company legal name, Swiss UID/IDE number, legal form (AG/SA), date of incorporation, registered office, place of effective management, shareholders, share capital, board composition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this return. The Swiss AG must disclose each non-resident legal owner. If a foreign entity has a Swiss permanent establishment, identify the Swiss PE address and the foreign head office and provide a power of attorney for a Swiss representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet (Bilanz): opening and closing assets and liabilities, including cash, trade receivables, container and bitumen inventory, prepayments, payables, provisions, paid-in share capital, legal reserves and retained earnings according to Swiss Code of Obligations accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the filing entity is a Swiss branch or permanent establishment of a non-resident company, report only the Swiss PE balance sheet; intercompany balances with the head office are adjusted for arm's-length terms and may require evidence of funding and interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account (Erfolgsrechnung): sales revenue from wholesale of drummed and bagged bitumen, cost of goods sold, gross margin, freight and logistics expenses, warehousing, salaries, depreciation, financial costs, extraordinary income and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income must be allocated to the Swiss tax presence in accordance with functions performed, assets owned and risks borne. A Swiss trading/wholesale function must document decision-making, contracts, LC issuance, Incoterms and risk management to justify the reported gross margin within the arm's-length range.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable profit (Berechnung des steuerbaren Reingewinns): accounting net profit adjusted for non-deductible expenses (taxes, fines, excessive board compensation, non-business gifts), deduction of tax-exempt items such as participation dividends and capital gains, and application of loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back Swiss corporate income tax itself and any non-deductible provision. Claim loss carryforwards up to the 7-year statutory period. A non-resident company trading through a Swiss branch must include only Swiss-source income and exclude head-office overheads not economically connected to the Swiss PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Equity statement for capital tax (Eigenkapitalnachweis): taxable equity base for cantonal and municipal capital tax, comprising paid-in share capital, disclosed and undisclosed reserves, retained earnings, and adjustments for hidden equity elements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss AG wholly owned by non-residents reports the full Swiss equity base. Shareholder loans structured as debt may be reclassified as equity for capital tax purposes where they bear entrepreneurial risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary annexes: form for participations, patent box, R&D super-deduction, transfer pricing disclosures, intercompany transaction schedule, and information on foreign permanent establishments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if Swiss annual turnover exceeds CHF 20 million or if significant intercompany transactions exist. A non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief must annex the Swiss withholding tax refund application Form 823A and the residence certificate (TRC) supporting the beneficial ownership claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or refusal to submit the corporate income tax return triggers procedural fines (Ordnungsbusse) under federal and cantonal law, typically up to CHF 1,000 federally and up to CHF 2,000 under cantonal procedure, plus default interest at the statutory rate (approximately 3.5%–5% per annum). There is no statutory daily surcharge, but deliberate non-filing may be prosecuted as tax evasion with a fine of up to three times the tax evaded.
